newsitem.title: GERMANY: Nestle German unit hit by blackmail bid.
newsitem.headline: Nestle German unit hit by blackmail bid.

text.p: Thomy, the German unit of food company Nestle, has received a blackmail letter carrying a warning that its products have been poisoned, Frankfurt police said late on Tuesday.
The German company, whose products include mustard and mayonnaise, has been targeted by blackmailers since August 1996.
Police said the company received a new letter on August 11 from a person claiming to have planted poisoned Nestle products in cities throughout Germany.

The blackmailer claimed to have deposited 23 poisoned food products four weeks ago in areas such as parking lots, buses, train stations and telephone kiosks in 12 German cities, including Berlin, Frankfurt, Munich, Cologne and Stuttgart.
He also claimed to have planted poisoned products at food shops in 14 cities nationwide.
Police said appropriate measures to protect consumers had been taken at the stores named in the letter.
There had not been any reports of poisoning from foodstuffs left in public areas, but police nonetheless advised that any products found should not be consumed.
Police in April discovered two tubes of mustard laced with cyanide in two separate German supermarkets, one in Saarbruecken in the southwest of Germany and one in Regensburg in the southeast.
Shoppers were urged to return all products bought in the shops in exchange for refunds.
